images.seen: Joburg highway gridlock under a massive purple storm, one lightning bolt over the skyline, wet lanes shining with brake lights. Monday.
lines: Lightning over the skyline and brake lights all the way in: Joburg is up early.
The slow lane, the fast lane, and the sky lane — only one is moving.
Somewhere a weather reporter is living their best life.

images.seen: A huge branched lightning strike over a modern estate street in rain, parked cars lit by the flash. Tuesday.
lines: That one landed close enough to count the seconds on one hand.
The whole street went daylight for a quarter of a second.
Every dog in the suburb filed a report at the same instant.

images.seen: Mammatus clouds glowing purple and pink over a windpomp and a sunflower field, orange horizon burning below. Wednesday.
lines: Those bubble clouds are the storm's signature, written on the way out.
That is the back page of a storm, and it reads better than the front.
The windpomp has seen a thousand of these and still stopped to look.

images.seen: A couple lying on the bedroom floor in soft morning light, coaxing a wide-eyed dachshund out from under the bed after the storm. Thursday.
lines: The storm passed an hour ago; the news has not reached under the bed yet.
The sky has moved on. The dachshund is requesting written confirmation.
The dog's under the bed. Smart move, honestly.
